description.one_line_summary: A store-picker sheet rises fast over a product page that dims and recedes, then takes nearly three times as long to hand the page back.
description.detailed_description: On a product detail page, tapping the link beside the store list raises a near-full-height sheet from the bottom in about 150 ms, decelerating into place with a grab handle at its top. While it rises the page behind dims under a grey veil and recedes slightly, iOS-modal style, so the sheet reads as being ON the page rather than replacing it. The sheet lists one row per store — logo, delivery estimate, price, availability — and one row is marked as chosen. Dismissal is not the reverse tempo: the sheet descends over roughly 420 ms, accelerating as it goes, and the veil lifts with it so the page is fully back only at the end. Neither direction overshoots.

motion_breakdown.start_state: Product page scrolled to the store list; no veil, page at full scale, sheet entirely below the viewport.
motion_breakdown.transition: Sheet translates up ~150 ms decelerating; backdrop veil fades in and host page recedes on the same clock. On dismiss the sheet translates down ~420 ms accelerating while the veil fades out and the page returns to scale.
motion_breakdown.end_state: Sheet off-screen, veil gone, page at full scale and scroll position untouched, with the chosen store row now highlighted in the list.
motion_breakdown.why_it_works: Arrival and return answer different questions. Arriving, the user has already decided to choose a store: the sheet must be there before the thought finishes, so 150 ms and no bounce. Returning, the user is being handed back a page they must re-find their place in, and the veil lifting slowly is what re-establishes it. Overshoot is refused in both directions because the sheet is a surface carrying a list to read, not an object arriving — a list that bounces past its stop reads as broken.

description.confidence_note: Both directions measured off 60 fps vertical kymographs, read by eye against the grid: onset and arrival are solid to ~2 frames (~33 ms), so the ratio is trustworthy and the absolute values are ±30 ms. The veil and recede timings were NOT measured separately — they are asserted to share the sheet's clock from the contact sheets, which is the weakest claim here.
